queue.t: [Down to watched-session pieces as of pass 518 — rim light on figures, a second foreground band, the empty band above the far layer (closed in pass 528: it was the foreground strip); the rest parked for a watched combat-readability call. Shipped unattended: fog 505, grade 507, room-light 509, foreground 510, ridge 511, light shafts 518.] Sean (2026-11-07): lighting and depth pass. The two worst independent-grade defects are flat lighting and depth collapse; Blasphemous and The Last Faith get their look from light that is part of the art and layered depth. Do: per-zone color grade and tint (CanvasModulate or equivalent), real light sources in rooms (PointLight2D or drawn glows: lanterns, windows, shrines, spell light) with directional light and rim light on figures, distance fog that fades parallax layers toward each zone's fog color, more parallax layers, and dark foreground silhouette layers that pass in front of the camera. Judge by eye at 1x and 2x with before/after screenshots across several zones; keep combat readable (foes and telegraphs must still pop). Covers the queued grade items on depth collapse. No PixelLab generations needed.
queue.why: Sean asked for it after comparing with Blasphemous and The Last Faith. Done so far: distance-fog colour (505), per-zone whole-scene grade (507), room light sources (509), foreground silhouette layers (510), a distant ridge parallax layer (511, the 'more parallax layers' piece). Still open: rim light on figures — the only remaining piece, and the one that most lifts the hero's read, but every figure is drawn procedurally with swapping dye/wash/dissolve materials, so a uniform rim needs a cross-cutting CanvasGroup per figure, best landed when its combat readability can be watched rather than in an unattended loop pass. (A further 'more parallax layers' option is a second, nearer foreground band.)

Independent grade (pass 585): rooms read as rectangular boxes again (Vorrhallow's flooded hall done in pass 587, the Sunken aqueduct in pass 588, the Spires storm ledge in pass 589; left: the Boughs canopy bridge): flat ceilings, straight walls and one thick tile border. Independent grade (pass 585): the hero is small, stiff and lower in contrast than a chest (camera, size and rim light are watched-session calls); smooth vector-like leaves and soft clouds behind crisp tiles (Boughs, Spires; parked pixel-grain call); the shop portrait is cruder than the sprites and the panel is plain (with the pass 584 shop item); the sword in the hit frames is a featureless white bar (watched feel call).

Spikes, the chest and foes fall below visible contrast, and the lantern clearings are coarse dithered blobs that read as a bug. Fog behind the play layer only, full value for platforms, pickups and foes, and a soft glow for lantern light (with the pass 570 and 555 fog items; held until the hydra and steam branches merge if they touch the Haar).

Independent grade (pass 580), what is left after pass 582 (twenty foes keep one bright color of their own, bible 12.69): the hero is about 6 percent of the screen height and foes are still small; the camera, sprite size and the rim light are watched-session calls (with the lighting item and the HD hero item). For the art loop when a base slot frees: the Bog Puffcap, the Bark Knight and the Spring Eel have no accent color on their sheets, so they got none; redraw each with one saturated part in a hue its body does not use, then give it a row in FoeLight.ACCENTS.

Thin it in front of the play layer and break the vertical smears (with the pass 555 drowned_stair item; held until the hydra and steam branches merge if they touch the Haar's fog).

From pass 572: the stalk's side roots still end in long thin tips, and the Evercrown's other halls (the Threshold, the Proving Scar) have no midground either.

Code-first: a lit surface line and depth gradient on the pool, a glow falloff on the lava, softer and sparser wind.

Independent grade (pass 565): both hit frames show the sword as a flat grey-white bar wider than the hero with no arc. The capture catches the hero's strike frame, the sheet's own blur of the blade (checked in pass 567); whether it should show an arc is the watched feel call found in pass 561 (the blow lands on the swing's first step; the smear waits for the strike frame). The struck foe's white cutout was closed in pass 567.

Art loop: PixelLab art for the seven placeholder guardians, Haar Wyrm first. Budget: 193 generations plus Sean's 50 USD of credits, all approved for this. Sean on facing (2026-11-06): strict east/west profile for anything that moves (walk, run, attacks, jumps); the south-east/south-west three-quarter stance, turned toward the camera, is welcome for animations where the figure stands still (idle, rest, talk, a guardian's intro or taunt). Update docs/art/enemy-style-guide.md (Facing, and 6 step 1a) to say so in the same PR, keep west as east mirrored, and give every character that has a still three-quarter clip a turn clip of 2 or 3 frames, generated in PixelLab from the three-quarter base (about one generation each), played forward from still to moving and backward from moving to still. Don't hand-fix drift in turn frames: Sean cleans those up himself. Copy each turn clip's frames to art/cleanup/<character>/turn/ for him, list the new ones on the workbench under "done" as ready for his cleanup, and have the importer prefer art/cleanup over the raw PixelLab output. Never overwrite or regenerate anything already in art/cleanup. Sean approves every base before animation (2026-11-06): for each new or redesigned character, make only its base first (the east profile and the south-east three-quarter stance, a few generations). Save one review picture to shots/<character>-base-for-approval.png: both views at 1x and 4x, next to the current in-game sprite and the hero for scale. Run python workbench/deploy.py (PYTHONUTF8=1) so it shows on the hosted Shots tab, and put "Waiting for Sean's OK on the <character> base" under "stuck". Generate no animations, turns included, for a character until a note from Sean approves its base. A note asking for changes means a retake of the base and a new review picture. While waiting, make bases for the next characters in the order (no more than three waiting at once) and otherwise do non-art work. Prompts for props (Sean, 2026-11-06: PixelLab once drew a light bulb on a figure's head when a stalk with an orb on its end was asked for): say what holds each prop and where it sits, one prop per sentence (Sean's wording that worked on the eel: "an anglerfish-style stalk with a dangling glowing orb"); scope a comparison to the part with "<creature>-style <part>", never "like a <creature>" or "like an anglerfish", which turns the whole body into that creature (the eel became a long skinny fish); keep a part's words physical (dangling, curving, fleshy) so it isn't read as an object, say what must stay clear when a prop could stray ("nothing on his head"), and give a glow a color rather than words like light, lamp or bulb. Check every base and frame for stray or moved props before anything goes to Sean. If a prop still wanders after one retake, generate the figure without it and add the prop with PixelLab's inpaint or the free pixelart_workbench, not more rerolls. Write these rules into the enemy style guide's prompt section in the same PR.

Independent grade (pass 497, 5.3/10, up from 4.1): top defect is the player sprite's fidelity gap. The hero reads as a small soft low-detail hooded blob with no readable silhouette or gear detail, far below the environment art (and below the guardians the art loop is remaking). Upgrade the player sprite's silhouette, detail and animation read so it is the most polished thing on screen, per design bible 13.5 (the hero is made in PixelLab). Judge at 1x and 2x against the enemy style guide.

Independent grade (pass 497): depth collapse and tile repetition. Trunks, mid platforms and the play layer share value and saturation, so the player gets lost against busy backdrops; brick and wall fields tile obviously. Strengthen atmospheric perspective (desaturate/darken the parallax back layers) so the play layer pops, and add tile variants so the grid's repeat unit stops reading.

Independent grade (pass 502): repetitive platform sprites. The same orange plank and rope-peg platform is tiled identically across unrelated zones (spires, sunken, tower, boughs), breaking each zone's material fiction. Give each zone its own platform/ledge material (stone, root, bone, crystal) so platforms belong to their world. Code-first in tilegen.

Independent grade (pass 502): zone-to-zone incoherence. The tilesets read as different kits with no shared palette, outline weight, or light direction, so the game looks like a sampler rather than one world. Unify the outline weight and the (top-left) light direction across zone tilesets and pull each zone's base hues toward the shared master palette. Code-first in tilegen.

Independent grade (pass 501): dead, oversized empty space. Several rooms (haar/drowned_stair, evercrown/heart, the Gnarlmaw arena) are dominated by huge flat backgrounds with a few thin platforms and nothing to look at. Add midground structures, props, light shafts and verticality (code-first in the room layouts + decor) so rooms feel authored, not empty boxes. Keep reachability/soft-lock tests passing.

Independent grade (pass 501): flat, directionless lighting. EdgeShade (pass 500) rims edges but scenes are still mostly uniform ambient fill; the few light sources (lanterns, candles) cast no falloff, bloom or coloured pools onto nearby geometry. Add directional key light + emissive glow with gradient falloff and contact shadow under platforms, code-first, for depth and focal hierarchy.

Independent grade (pass 501): enemies camouflaged against their tiles. The green grasshopper reads into green foliage (boughs) and the green knight into blue-grey walls (vorrhallow); red spike hazards barely separate from decor. Give foes and hazards a reserved accent colour or outline that never appears in the background palette so threats pop. Code-first.

Independent grade (pass 510): UI/art style clash. The coarse-pixel shop panels and HUD read 8-bit/placeholder next to the finer hi-res in-world tiles and backdrops, breaking cohesion (grade area 'UI and menus' 5.5). Code-first in the UI drawing (PixelFont/menus/shop panels): lift the panel framing, spacing and chrome to match the in-world art's density, or deliberately commit to a crisp diegetic style, so the UI stops reading as a stub. Judge at 1x against the enemy style guide and a shop screenshot.

[Attempted pass 523 as a D-grid far-layer snap (collapse each 2x2 texture cell to one colour so the far layers share the foreground's whole-world-pixel grain); regressed by eye - vertical-fibre zones were fine but thin diagonal linework and soft clouds (Boughs) eroded into dashed, speckled branches with 2x2 sky noise. Needs per-painter tuning and a watched aesthetic eye; parked like rim light and the letterbox band - do not re-attempt unattended.] Independent grade (pass 520): painterly backdrops vs hard pixel foreground. The anti-aliased/painterly far backdrops (boughs, sunken, evercrown) sit behind chunky hard-edged pixel tiles, so the frame reads as two media. Hold one dither language across depths: bring the far layers' edges/dither into the pixel grid (or push the foreground softer) so background and foreground read as one hand-drawn world. (Partly chipped from the tile side in pass 520; this is the backdrop half.)

Independent grade (pass 545): the Sunken Spring's rock pillars read as stacked sine-stripe wallpaper with blue squiggles, and its water is a flat teal fill: redraw the pillars as stone (cracks, ledges, ragged silhouettes) and give the water a depth gradient, caustics and a lit surface line.

Independent grade (pass 545): wading foes in Vorrhallow are cut by a flat translucent water rectangle; draw a ripple line and splash at each waterline. Rain in the Spires is uniform white dashes over everything; layer it, sparser and dimmer in front.

Independent grade (pass 550), the half left after pass 552 (the seal now burns in tall licks with a glow falloff): over half of the Proving Scar's opening frame is solid mass sunk into the dark by DeepShade (12.38). A room-layout item: open the mass with a chamber or a far window, or give deep stillglass rock its own veins.

Follow-on to pass 554: use the item icons (UiArt) on the Equipment and Inventory pages, and consider the portraits in the dialogue box (bible 12.44 and 13.3). Code only; the pictures already exist for every item and every person with a look.

It needs a new wall-base tile and a rule in TilesetFactory; low value, do it only with other tile-rule work.

Tooling (found in pass 558): tools/art/decorgen.py seeds each zone by its name (random.Random(zone)), so the zones renamed in pass 462 (the Haar, Vorrhallow, the Evercrown and others) no longer regenerate to their committed decor atlases; a whole run redraws them. Pass 558 regenerated only the Evercrown's. Either pin a seed number per zone that reproduces the committed art, or regenerate every atlas once, look at each, and commit them together.

Found in pass 561's fight frames, for a watched feel call (do not change unattended): a blow lands on the swing's first step and the hitstop holds on the windup pose; the blade and its smear travel only afterwards (the smear has waited for the strike frame since pass 537). At the instant of impact there is a spark and a flash but no arc. Also the hero's swing frame carries a wide pale blade blur across his torso that reads heavier than the crescent.

Tooling (found in pass 563): a whole run of tools/art/tilegen.py rewrites five mid layers that this pass did not touch (boughs, haar, hearthroot, heartwood, trials), so the committed pictures no longer match the painters or a painter is not deterministic. Find which (run it twice and compare), then either fix the seed or regenerate, look at each and commit them together.

Tooling (found in pass 563): every checkout and worktree shares user://, so a test run in another worktree (Yldenfall-crouch, Yldenfall-steam) writes test saves that this run's leak check reports as 'saves changed (save_8.json)'; three reachability tests failed that way and pass alone. Give the test runner its own save folder per process, or have the leak check ignore files it did not see its own test write.

Tooling (found in pass 570): test_every_room_loads_and_settles_inside_the_budget measures wall-clock time, so it fails whenever another session is busy on this PC (six runs in pass 570 failed on six different sets of rooms; CI passes). Measure each room against a calibration room loaded in the same run, or retry a room that misses before failing it. Pass 572 (2026-11-15): it failed ten local runs in a row at 71% to 88% CPU from other sessions and passed on the eleventh; evercrown/proving_scar is always the first over (511 to 909 ms against 500), so that room sits nearest the load budget.

Audio (from passes 569 and 570): the Bell Loft's fallen bell and the Gear Pit's gears are silent. A cracked, dead clank when the bell is struck, and a dull iron knock on each of the gears' two bites, heard only in the room.

From pass 584: running tools/art/tilegen.py on this PC rewrites boughs_mid, haar_mid, hearthroot_mid, heartwood_mid and trials_mid with bytes that differ from the committed pictures, though none of their painters changed (last committed in pass 462). Find whether the generator drifted from them or is not byte-stable across machines, compare the pictures by eye, and add a guard (test_tilegen.py) that the committed backdrops match what the generator makes.

Audio (from pass 631): Carillon's far lightning is silent. A low, distant roll of thunder a beat after each stroke (RainLanding.stroke_start), quiet under the rain, heard only in the Spires and never once the Sky Spring has broken the storm. Needs a new sound in tools/audio/sfxgen.py and a pass of tools/audio/levels.py --check.

It is one body value cut by tapered grain streaks that end, joined across every seam; the tier blends cut wood into blobs (the first full suite caught the Haar's blend). Each roofed side exit now darkens toward the edge as a passage running on under the wall, behind the tiles and actors (ExitMouth, bible 12.125). Full suite: 37,134 passed; 17 failed only on the save guard because the played build kept writing save_2.json (proved with no tests running); each passed its own checks alone. CI green. It is lit by the far rim now, and two rows of faceted crystal masses (lit west facet, dark east, glints) grow up through it in the Evercrown and Vorrhallow (bible 12.124). Full suite 37,116 checks, all passed; CI green. Room pictures refreshed. Next: walls that end mid-air at the screen's edge.

Over the full shade it now shows its zone's buried matter faintly: roots hanging in the woods and the marsh, zigzag crystal veins in the crystal halls, bedding seams in the stone zones (bible 12.123). The first suite caught a load-budget overrun in trials/stillness (502 ms); forms are capped at 60 a room and the build costs at most 14 ms. Full suite 37,116 checks, all passed; CI green. Room pictures refreshed. The Evercrown veins' flat purple (the ridge's solid near plane) is next.

The pass 645 grade (5.2) no longer names it.

done.why: The Tower's mid girders ran roof to floor and Vorrhallow's colonnade nearly so. Room pictures refreshed.

done.why: The pass 640 grade saw the same pine band behind five areas; the Heartwood shared the High Boughs' firs. Its ridge is now great arching roots, the far layer through each arch (bible 12.118). The trunk columns are next.

done.why: The pass 630 grade's Heartwood tell. Resumed after an app restart and merged; fight pictures refreshed.

done.t: Pass 632: a soft light and a gust, not dither and dashes (PR #713)
done.why: The pass 630 grade's first new item: 'a square of magenta dither round the foe in the flooded hall, white dash clusters in the canopy sky'. The square was the Crystal Dwarf's FoeGlow (four tones through a coarse dither); it now falls off in 14 fine tones on a steeper curve and reads as a soft pocket of light. The dashes were the High Boughs' wind; each is now a gust that brightens from a faint tail to its head downwind, bowed a pixel, fewer of them, over a wash that fades at its edges (bible 12.108). Not done: the Inner Rings' currents were not looked at one by one; the Haar's lava pillar and lamp halos stay held with the fog. Full suite 33,551 of 33,552: the wall-clock room-load budget failed once (evercrown/proving_scar 515 ms against 500, the known flake) and passed three times alone; CI passed. The Boughs, Trials and Vorrhallow rooms and three fight frames recaptured.

done.t: Pass 631: rain lands, and lightning lights the stone (PR #712)
done.why: The pass 625 grade's next item: 'the rain is one even overlay with no splash or wet stone, and the lightning lights nothing'. Every Spires room now builds a RainLanding: tops open to the sky carry a broken line of wet sheen and splashes (a top under an overhang or a board stays dry), and every 3 to 11 seconds a far stroke lifts the sky behind the ground and rims every wet top, so the room's mass stands dark against a lit sky (bible 12.107). The stroke follows the flashes option and stops once the Sky Spring breaks the storm. Not done: thunder (queued), light on figures, rain on the scenery islands. Full suite 33,365 of 33,365 with no rerun; CI passed. The nine Spires rooms and the two Spires fight frames recaptured. No grade this pass (the next is due after pass 635).

done.t: Pass 630: what you can still use catches the light (PR #711)
done.why: The pass 625 grade's next item: 'chests, signs and pickups do not separate from the scenery'. A zone's chest and stele are built in the zone's own stone, so they vanished into it. A closed chest now has a stepped halo, a rim in its accent along the top of its silhouette and a glint; an opened chest has none, so what is left to do reads from across the room. A stele has the halo and the rim in its inlay's color (bible 12.106). Item pickups were left, and the Haar's chest is still under the fog (held). Full suite 33,290 of 33,293 checks in the whole run; the three were the wall-clock budget flake and both tests passed on rerun; CI passed. Room (127), fight and shop pictures recaptured. Independent grade: 5.1 with a fresh, strict grader (5.6 at pass 625); chests and signs are no longer named.

done.t: Pass 629: a zone builds its own post (PR #710)
done.why: The pass 625 grade's next item: 'the same cross-braced plank platform in nearly every frame, recoloured'. The frames already differed by zone, so what repeated was the upright squared post. Each zone family now builds its own (bible 12.105): raked sawhorse legs in the Heartwood, cut limbs in the Boughs, piles with heads above the deck in the Haar and the Sunken Spring, iron columns set in from the board's ends in the Tower and the Trials, stone piers in the Spires and Vorrhallow; the town keeps the squared post. The board itself is still one straight plank tile per zone. Full suite 32,925 checks, 0 failed; CI passed; room pictures recaptured (127). The next independent grade is due after pass 630.

done.t: Pass 628: a ceiling is a few large shapes, not a row of teeth (PR #709)
done.why: The pass 625 grade's first item, the last of it: terrain had 'no large form'. The storm ledge's overhang was four equal notches, the canopy bridge three knots a tile apart, the flooded hall's fallen vault a comb. Each now has one form plainly the largest, and a ceiling's underside may turn once in seven columns at most, checked in every room (bible 12.104). Only ceilings changed. The slopes are still 45 degrees: a second pitch is queued. Full suite 32,859 checks, 0 failed; CI passed; room pictures recaptured (127).

done.t: Pass 627: the top of the ground is not a ruled line (PR #708)
done.why: The pass 625 grade's first item, the rest of it: terrain had 'no top-lip variation'. Every floor ended in one level line and every ledge in a square corner. TopLip now grows moss hummocks (2 to 7 texels) on walking surfaces and drapes moss over the end of a ledge, in the zone's own cap tones, in the eight moss-capped zones (bible 12.103). Small at 1x. Full suite 32,664 checks, 0 failed; CI passed; room pictures recaptured (127).

done.t: Pass 626: mass that hangs over open air is in shadow (PR #707)
done.why: The pass 625 grade's first item: terrain had 'no shadowed underside'. A ceiling's lowest course was its lightest tier, as bright as a lit floor. SoffitShade now puts ground with open air under it in full shade, holds half shade through the mass above, and feathers into the wall; walking surfaces, floors and slopes keep their light. Baked into one texture per room. Full suite 32,536 checks, 0 failed; CI passed; room pictures recaptured (127).

done.t: Pass 625: a zone's rooms do not share one scaffold, one island or one view (PR #706)
done.why: The pass 620 grade named 'the same scaffold and floating island across zones'. Every room of a zone opened on the same spot of its backdrop, so the storm ledge and the Fallen Bridge showed the same islands in the same places: each room now slides the far, ridge and mid layers its own way. A sky island comes in four builds (wedge, shelf, fang, twin). The Boughs stand a board on forked limbs still in leaf and the Spires on stone corbels and piers; the Heartwood keeps the lashed frame. Full suite 32,484 checks passed and one wall-clock budget check (8.27 ms against 8) failed, then passed twice alone; CI green. Room and fight pictures recaptured. Independent grade after the pass: 5.6 of 10, level; the islands are no longer named, the plank on posts still is. No PixelLab generations spent; the three guardian bases still wait for Sean.

done.t: Pass 624: props are not copies of each other (PR #705)
done.why: The pass 620 grade named copied props: 'one crystal cluster at several angles in the flooded hall, identical banners in the plaza'. Hearthroot had one banner picture; it has three now (a red swallowtail, a long blue pennon, a torn market cloth). A decor piece that would repeat a neighbour of its kind within five cells takes the next picture. Vorrhallow's backdrop stillglass was one build (a leader and a fan) turned and scaled; it grows in four habits now (spray, blade, druse, twin), no two in a row alike. Full suite 32,319 checks, CI green. Room pictures recaptured. Left: the scaffold and floating island across zones. No PixelLab generations spent; the three guardian bases still wait for Sean.

done.t: Pass 623: a tier ends block by block (PR #704)
done.why: The pass 620 grade called brick and earth 'large rectangular dark blotches and stair-stepped tone patches that read as tile errors' (aqueduct, canopy bridge, flooded hall, storm ledge). The cause was the wall tiers: three flat values a whole shade apart that met along the tile grid. Every generated tileset now has six blend tiles in which each brick, bark plate or cobble stands in one of two neighbouring tiers, and a room draws them where two tiers meet; a patch of other stone is no longer drawn dark inside a lit pier. Big blocks (Vorrhallow, the Tower) blend in soft blobs: whether that is too mottled is for Sean to judge in play. Room captures are refreshed. Full suite 32,053 checks, CI green.

done.t: Pass 622: the Spires' skyline is a ruined city on a hill (PR #703)
done.why: The pass 615 grade called the storm ledge's far skyline a flat one-value silhouette: every spire was one pole in one tone, driven through a hill of one tone (one color held 73 percent of the far plane). A spire is now a needle, a notched crown, a tower sheared off at a slant or a keep on a broad base, each with a wall tone of its own and shaded round; bridges on pointed arches join some, every other one fallen; the hill steps down in terraces; the nearer row no longer wears pale caps of mist. Bible 12.98, tests/test_spires_skyline.gd (four tests; three fail against the old picture). Full suite 30,713 checks passed, 0 failed; CI passed on the second run (the first failed a chance bound in pass 621's chips test: a chip had to leap 8 px in four frames and the slowest, steepest one covers 6.5; now 5). The Spires' nine room pictures and two fight frames are recaptured. For Sean to judge in play: whether the row is too busy behind a fight. Not done: the near row is still one tone under its lit walls.

done.t: Pass 621: a blow knocks chips off the foe (PR #702)
done.why: The pass 615 grade called a landed hit one small spark with no foe flash, streak or debris in the frame. A blow that wounds now breaks splinters off the body in the foe's own colors, read off its sheet (6, or 10 from a heavy blow), thrown on along the blow; the hit-stop holds them with the spark, and a turned blow sheds none. No number of the fight changed. The fight pictures were taken on the frame the 0.08 s flash ended; they are now taken one frame earlier. Bible 6.7, tests/test_hit_chips.gd (three tests, five mutations caught). Full suite 30,704 checks passed, 0 failed; CI passed. The 11 fight pictures are recaptured. For Sean to judge in play: whether the chips are too many on fast combos. Not done: the flash's length (the watched feel call); code-drawn guardians shed pale bone, not their own colors.

done.t: Pass 620: the water meets the stone (PR #701)
done.why: The pass 615 grade called the water a slab of banded dither with a hard top line and no meeting with the stone. The deep water's surface is now a swell with a sheen and glints, dim under a roof; water laps a square face of stone with foam and a damp line; stone that stands in water is darkened toward teal at its faces (12 px, four steps); and the body has eight tones where it had five. Vorrhallow's still water laps and darkens its stone too. Bible 12.97, tests/test_water_edge.gd (six tests, mutation-checked). Full suite 30,661 checks passed, 0 failed; CI passed. Room, fight and arena pictures are recaptured. Not done: a mirror image of the room on the surface; foam where a slope enters the water; a waterline on bodies in deep water. Independent grade after it: 5.6 of 10, level; the water is no longer named.

done.t: Pass 619: a fire seal lights the stone round it (PR #700)
done.why: The pass 615 grade called the Marsh Road's seal a lava column with no glow falloff onto what is round it. A seal now lights the lip of the stone that looks at it (gold on the lip, red behind it, stepping down along the floor, the arch and a wall out to 44 px), burns with a gold spine and red flanks, and gives off embers. Bible 12.96. Four new tests, each mutation-checked; full suite 30,613 checks passed, 0 failed; CI passed. The Marsh Road, Proving Scar and West Gate pictures and the Haar fight frames are recaptured. Not done: the halo's dither and the fog over it (held).

done.t: Pass 618: a tier has no specks (PR #699)
done.why: Seen in pass 614 and named with the pass 615 grade: lone dark tiles sit inside lit wall fields (the Flooded Hall's ceiling, the storm ledge). The louder cause was Vorrhallow's atlas: a worn block there is half a tile, and with four tiles to a tier every fourth tile of a field was a dark slab. A field tile now wears only its half blocks and the deep tier none, so each tier is one value (deep 40.5 to 41.6, where it ran 30 to 41). And a group of fewer than three cells of a darker tier takes the tier above (four specks in the three named rooms). Bible 12.95, tests/test_tier_specks.gd (four tests, mutation-checked). All 127 room pictures are recaptured. Not done: a tier's edge still steps by the tile (softening it needs drawn transition tiles, a watched look); the gym's brick keeps its spread.

done.t: Pass 617: the town's skyline is a row of houses (PR #698)
done.why: Pass 610 grade: the plaza skyline's gridded windows; pass 615 grade: far skylines are flat one-value silhouettes. Hearthroot's ridge was flat-topped blocks under one lattice of windows. Each house now has a roof of its own (a gable, a hip, a lean-to or a tower, some with a chimney), one of four wall tones, a lit west roof slope and a dark east one, and a few windows of its own; 48 lit windows where the lattice showed 80. Bible 12.94, tests/test_town_skyline.gd (three tests, all fail on the old picture). The seven Hearthroot room pictures are recaptured. For Sean to judge in play: whether the houses, tall under their eaves, read as a hill town or as towers. Not done: the Spires' ridge and the nearer plane.

done.t: Pass 616: a ware is weighed against what you wear (PR #697)
done.why: Pass 610 and 615 grades: the shop panel has a large dead area and no comparison with equipped gear. The chosen ware now stands to one side of the shop's counter, and a table fills the rest: yours, an arrow, the ware's, and a mark that points up (better) or down (worse). Gear is weighed against what you wear in its place, a temper against your blade, keys and belt things against how many you carry. Bible 12.93, test_a_ware_is_weighed_against_what_you_wear. The 21 shop pictures are recaptured. For Sean to judge in play: whether a one-line comparison (the Tanned Jerkin) sits too far from its label. Not done: the keepers' portraits, and the Equipment page could take the same table.

done.t: Pass 615: a bough's bark is plates (PR #696)
done.why: Pass 610 grade: the canopy zone's terrain is flat vertical brown stripes. The High Boughs' tiles were the Heartwood's two-value strands. A bough's bark is now plates of one value between dark furrows that slant, fork and join, on one wrapped layout so no seam cuts a plate; the trim is notched at a furrow. The Heartwood and the Haar keep their strands. Bible 12.92, tests/test_bough_bark.gd. Rooms and fight pictures recaptured. Independent grade after it: 5.6, level with pass 610, and the stripes are no longer named.

done.t: Pass 614: a wall is relaid in patches (PR #695)
done.why: Pass 610 grade: uniform brick fields in the Flooded Hall, the storm ledge and the aqueduct. Every tile of a zone had the same course heights, so a long wall was one texture. Vorrhallow, the Spires and the Sunken Spring each have a second coursing now (small brick, great blocks, thin courses), laid in wide, low stretches inside the walls, with a joint where a patch stops (bible 12.91). Room pictures refreshed. For Sean to judge in play: whether Vorrhallow's small brick reads as a repair or as noise. Seen and queued: the darker tiers step by the tile.

done.t: Pass 613: a fill grows in patches (PR #694)
done.why: Pass 610 grade: one vine overlay on every block (the plaza). Hearthroot's walls were filled from one 128 px texture with roots and moss on every block, repeating every four tiles. The fill is now 16 tiles across and the growth lives in patches; elsewhere a root keeps its shape in the stone's own color, as a carving (bible 12.90). Room and shop pictures refreshed. For Sean to judge in play: whether the carved roots read as relief or as shadow. Left for the next pass: the painted brick fields of the Flooded Hall, the storm ledge and the aqueduct.

done.t: Pass 612: a foe's body is lit by a fill (PR #693)
done.why: Pass 610 grade: foes sink into dark rooms (the Rot Dwarf against the trunk, the Flooded Hall's foe a dark smudge). The room's light had sunk a foe's body to the value of its room's shadows. A foe's mid tones now take a fill in the zone's own light; the outline, lights, tell and accent are unchanged, and nothing is drawn round the figure (bible 12.89). Room and fight pictures refreshed. For Sean to judge in play: whether foes now read too bright for the muted rooms. The hero is unchanged (his rim light is a watched call).

done.t: The Haar Wyrm on a skeleton (PR #691; colors and flash fix in PR #692)
done.why: Sean asked whether a rig would beat drawing every frame, saw the prototype and said to finish it. The Wyrm is now his PixelLab head, body and neck art on a Skeleton2D: telescoping necks that follow the fight, his shadowed heads for the reveal, steam, drips and the throat glow. The fight is unchanged. Clips: haar-wyrm-rig-*.gif. Bible 8.4 and the new 13.7 (when to rig a guardian).

done.t: Pass 611: a tell gathers on the weapon (PR #690)
done.why: Pass 610 grade: the Rot Dwarf's tell in the Heartwood read as a flat yellow full-body tint, like a debug overlay. A sheet foe now keeps its own colors in a wind-up: a four-point glint gathers on its weapon and the gold rim is drawn only near it (22 foes, bible 12.88). Fight pictures refreshed. For Sean to judge in play: whether the glint warns as fast as the whole-body pulse did.

done.t: Pass 610: a bounce-pod is a ripe gourd (PR #689)
done.why: Pass 605 grade: the 'flat green placeholder block' in the Canopy Bridge was the bounce-pod, drawn as plain rectangles. It is now a pixel-drawn pale gold gourd in green sepals (bible 12.87). Room pictures refreshed. Independent grade after it: 5.6 of 10 (5.3).

done.t: Pass 609: no clock face (PR #688)
done.why: Pass 605 grade: the hit spark read as a clock-face lock-on marker. The VFX sheets' ring, ticks and crosshair spikes are gone (tools/art/sparkfix.py): the star burns down and the sparks fly forward and fall. Fight pictures refreshed.

done.t: Pass 608: a plain zero (PR #687)
done.why: Pass 605 grade: the gold counter's slashed zero read as a debug glyph. The pixel font's 0 is now a plain oval, one column narrower than O. Shop pictures refreshed.

done.t: Retired the hosted workbench (Sean, 2026-11-18)
done.why: Its sync (push.py) posted the whole live state to Vercel every minute and spent most of the account's 10 GB transfer allowance, all failing since the Blob store was suspended. push.py, deploy.py and workbench/vercel are removed; the workbench is local only.

done.t: Pass 607: a struck foe stays solid (PR #685)
done.why: Pass 605 grade: the struck foe read as a see-through ghost. The soft phase of a hit flash is now 0.3 of a warm cream instead of 0.45 of white, so a foe keeps its own colors. The loop is paused after this pass (Sean, 2026-11-18).

done.t: Pass 606: health is a sprig of leaves (PR #683)
done.why: Pass 605 grade: the health masks copied Hollow Knight's. Health is now amber autumn leaves, and every player-facing 'mask' says leaf. A picture went to Sean for his OK.

done.t: Pass 605: the shop is a place (PR #682)
done.why: Pass 600 grade: the shop was a plain box, two-thirds empty. Every menu is framed with gold brackets, and a shop of few wares shows the chosen one on a lit counter. Independent grade after it: 5.3 of 10 (5.2 at pass 600).

done.t: Pass 604: each zone builds its own trestle (PR #681)
done.why: Pass 600 grade: the same X-braced trestle repeated across zones. Each family now frames its plank runs its own way: lashed timber, pilings, an iron truss, a stone arch, grown sinew; the town keeps the trestle.

done.t: Pass 603: the minimap shows the ways on (PR #680)
done.why: Pass 600 grade: the minimap was an empty panel with one rectangle and the HUD a plain box. The minimap now shows the map's grid, door openings and stubs for the ways on, and shares gold corner brackets with the HUD's plate.

done.t: Pass 602: a struck foe keeps its edge (PR #679)
done.why: Pass 600 grade: the struck foe read as going see-through. Through a hit flash a sheet foe now wears a near-black rim one pixel wide, so its pale body stays parted from the white cut.

done.t: Pass 601: the Spires stand on a ridge of their own (PR #678)
done.why: Pass 600 grade: the town's window-dotted skyline repeated in the Spires. The Spires now stand on ruined spires: tall narrow towers with slit windows.

done.t: Pass 600: the pictures show the game as played (PR #677)
done.why: Pass 595 grade: no HUD in the captures. Fight frames now keep the HUD; a tilegen run leaves unchanged pictures alone. Independent grade after it: 5.2 of 10 (5.3 at pass 595).

done.t: Pass 599: the struck foe reads through the cut (PR #676)
done.why: Pass 595 grade: in hit frames the slash and spark covered the struck foe. The impact streak now runs behind the actors and comes out past the body, and a struck foe draws above the swing's smear for 0.2 s.

done.t: Pass 598: the ridge gains a body, and the town its light (PR #675)
done.why: Pass 595 grade: the parallax ridges were flat silhouettes with empty stretches. Every ridge now steps into two planes under valley mist, with lit faces and its zone's distant detail (houses with windows, rock ledges, crystal clefts), and Hearthroot's far town is lit under warm roofs.

done.t: Pass 597: a floating stone hangs on its keel (PR #674)
done.why: Pass 595 grade: the Spires' floating bridge stones now hang on keels of sky-island rock with drifting pebbles, and the flooded hall's stillglass lights its own pillar and chips the stone where it breaks through. Next: the flat midground and parallax layers (plaza, gear pit, flooded hall).

done.t: Pass 596: a plank stands on a built trestle (PR #673, merged)
done.why: The pass 595 grade: platforms read as bare debug-like sticks on posts (plaza, gear pit, causeway). Posts are now 4 px squared timber with a cap block, knee brackets, a footing stone and bolts in the zone accent; two posts under a run are tied by a rail and cross-braced bay by bay. Bible 12.81; room pictures refreshed.

done.t: Pass 595: every zone houses its own chest (PR #672, merged)
done.why: The pass 585 grade: the same chest in nearly every room. One brown trunk stood in all 68 chest cells; now eight kinds by zone: a root coffer with moss and roots (Heartwood), a woven hamper (Boughs), a driftwood sea chest with rope and barnacles (Haar), a riveted dwarf strongbox in each zone's metal (Hearthroot, Sunken, Vorrhallow), an ore crate (Tower), a sandstone reliquary with a pitched roof (Spires), a geode casket with crystal shards (Evercrown), and the trunk (gym, Trials). All in the master palette; bible 12.80. Then the independent grade: 5.3, level, combat readability up to 5.5.

done.t: Pass 594: a menu names its keys (PR #671, merged)
done.why: The pass 590 grade: the shop's odd 'Jump: choose / Dash: leave' labels. Every menu now ends with key caps, the bound key or pad button in a framed cap, then a verb for what it does there: a shop says Buy and Leave, the skill tree Learn, the lift Ride, the pause menu Resume. Bible 12.79; test_a_menu_names_its_keys_and_what_they_do; full suite 19,310 checks, CI green. Shop pictures refreshed.

done.t: Pass 593: the thorn bulbs stop reading as strawberries (PR #670, merged)
done.why: The pass 590 grade: the red thorn rows read as strawberries or candy. Each pod is now a dark woody husk split by a pulsing ember seam, with five long outlined bone thorns and a bark vine instead of a green stem. Bible 12.32; test_thorn_the_husk_is_dark_and_bristles; full suite 19,290 checks, CI green. Room pictures refreshed.

done.t: Pass 592: the cut is laid across the foe, and the foe reels (PR #669, merged)
done.why: The pass 590 grade: combat readability 4.5, the spark small and the struck foe with no knockback pose. Every hit spark now lays a tapered white impact streak across the foe for 0.16 s, and the 22 sheet-drawn foes lean away from the blow through their hitstun. Bible 6.7; tests/test_hit_impact.gd; full suite 18,630 checks, CI green. Fight pictures refreshed.

done.t: Pass 591: a vault curves into its wall, the haunches (PR #667)
done.why: The pass 590 grade's first defect: the four reshaped rooms' ceilings read as stair-stepped tile blocks. Every painted atlas gains the ceiling's 45-degree slopes (legend ` and '), drawn from each zone's ceiling tile, colliding as triangles; tools/levels/haunches.py laid 28 to 33 into the Canopy Bridge, Flooded Hall, Drowned Aqueduct and Storm Ledge. Bible 12.78.

done.t: Pass 590: the Canopy Bridge crosses a hollow in the crown (PR #666)
done.why: The last of the four box rooms the pass 585 grade named: a ragged canopy with tapering knots above the wind band, bulging trunk walls, and the chest on a bough grown from the east trunk instead of a rope-hung plank. Bible 12.77. Independent grade after it: 5.3/10.

done.t: Pass 589: the Storm Ledge lies under a broken island (PR #665, merged)
done.why: The third box room from the pass 585 grade: a ragged overhang open to the storm with two hanging spurs, bulging walls, and the chest on a crag instead of a plank table. Bible 12.76; full suite 18,268 checks passed.

done.t: Pass 588: the Drowned Aqueduct is vaulted, and its arches have broken (PR #664)
done.done: Squash-merged de81d5ef. The second of the four box rooms from the pass 585 grade. Its three bays are vaulted, springing low from the hanging piers and the walls; the piers' feet are broken off; the four arch tops are broken wedges over their piers' stumps on the bed, with room to swim between; each wall has a buttress and the gallery a corbel. The broken channel's fall, the doors, eels, shard and chest are unmoved (bible 12.75). Next: the Spires storm ledge, then the Boughs canopy bridge.

done.t: Pass 587: the Flooded Hall is vaulted, and its east vault has fallen (PR #663)
done.done: Squash-merged f076a9c6. The pass 585 grade called four rooms rectangular boxes; the Flooded Hall is the first. Its two bays are vaulted with a rib between, each pillar has a capital and a broken foot, the east vault has fallen in (a hanging voussoir at its edge), and the fallen stone lies in the water as a heap with the chest on top: no more thin table in this hall (bible 12.74). The drains test now frees each world (it had read the previous hall's ground). For Sean in play: is the chest too easy now, a walk up the heap? Next: the Sunken aqueduct, then the Spires storm ledge and the Boughs canopy bridge.

done.t: Pass 586: the rim carries the tell (PR #662)
done.why: A sheet foe's tell is the gold rim plus a light tint (SHEET_TELL 0.2), so its colors and pose read; code-drawn guardians keep the 0.45 wash (no rim). Skyrend's tell is in the fight set. For Sean in play: does the rim alone warn as fast?

done.t: Pass 585: a tell keeps the foe's pose (PR #660)
done.done: Squash-merged 3b0b84e3. The pass 575 and 580 grades called each tell frame a flat white silhouette, 'like a missing texture'. A tell's pulse is now a warm gold tint that leaves more than half of the foe's own contrast (Enemy.TELL_TINT, SHEET_TELL 0.42, TELL_WASH 0.45), with a one-pixel gold rim on a foe drawn from a sheet; white is kept for a blow that lands (bible 6.7 and 12.72). The beat, length and sound of every tell are unchanged. The Grub Lump, the Lantern Ghost and the Spring Eel now soften their hit flash like the rest. Full suite 1198 tests, 18144 checks, 0 failed; CI test and mix passed. Fight frames recaptured. For Sean to judge in play: whether gold warns as fast as white did. Independent grade after it: 5.3 (5.6 at pass 580, a fresh grader each time); combat readability 5.5, up from 5.2.

done.t: Pass 584: Carillon's storm stands behind the fight (PR #659)
done.done: Squash-merged 0f1bdd75. The pass 580 grade called the Spires fight frame noisy. The rain's near layer is at alpha 0.46 (was 0.85) and the far one at 0.26, with a cap of 0.5; the bolts baked into the far sky are dim violet threads (they were white and never went out); the sky, storm banks and far limbs are a step darker. Lightning in play is unchanged, so bright lightning now always means something. Bible 12.71. For Sean to judge in play: if the storm now feels too light, SheetRain.LAYERS is the one place to raise it. Full suite 18109 checks, 0 failed (a first run failed 44 checks because the working copy of the bible had CRLF line endings; a fresh checkout passed); CI passed. Room, arena and fight pictures recaptured. No PixelLab generations spent.

done.t: Pass 583: sheets and blocks run through the tile seams (PR #658)
done.done: Squash-merged e7d251f6. The pass 580 grade named tile repetition that shows the grid. The Tower's plates are now sheets one to three tiles long: half the tiles of every scattered set have no west seam, so the sheet from the west runs through them. The Spires' ashlar has one set of courses in every tile and no head joint near a tile's edge, so blocks pass through the seams and a wall is one wall (it was a quilt of 16 px patches); fewer cracks and worn blocks. Bible 12.70. The Tower's change is the quieter one: horizontal seams still run every tile. Full suite 18101 checks, 0 failed; CI passed. Room, arena and fight pictures recaptured. No PixelLab generations spent.

done.t: Pass 582: each foe keeps one color of its own (PR #657)
done.done: Squash-merged 752b06dd. The pass 580 grade called foes dark on dark and asked for one saturated color each. The room's light (bible 12.43) muted a foe's accent with its body; now a band of hue on the foe's own sheet is left out of the mute and lifted (bible 12.69): the Rot Dwarf's orange cloth, the Grub Lump's cyan spots, the Iron Dwarf's bronze edges, the Minecart Rider's gloves and cart bands, and so on for twenty foes. Five have none: the Lantern Ghost (faint by design), the Crystal Dwarf (it has its glow), and the Bog Puffcap, the Bark Knight and the Spring Eel (no such color on their sheets; queued for the art loop). The hit flash, the tell and the death are unchanged. For Sean to judge in play: it is a small lift at 1x; a foe is as large and as dark as it was, with one bright part. Full suite: 1,190 tests, 17,662 checks, all passed; CI test and mix passed. Room and fight pictures and the catalogue refreshed. Next independent grade: after pass 585.

done.t: Pass 581: the stalk's roots heaved the Veins' floor, and the vault steps down to its walls (PR #656)
done.done: Squash-merged a27e8ad2. The Veins are no longer a plain box (bible 12.68), the sixth and last room the pass 575 grade's room-shape item named, so that item is closed. The floor stands at three heights: a hump one tile high between the west door's landing and the stalk, the stalk's own floor as it was, a bank a tile up east of it and a bank two up against the east wall, all by ramps, so the foot is a walk.
